cues: Do not confuse Peltier heat with Joule heat.
Peltier heat happens only at a junction of two different metals; Joule heat in any conductor.
Peltier heat goes as I; Joule heat as I squared.
Reverse the current, and Peltier heating becomes cooling; Joule heating stays heating.
Peltier can cool a junction below room temperature; Joule never can.
For completeness, there is a third effect, the Thomson effect, along a single wire with a temperature gradient.
It is zero for lead, which is why lead is used as the reference metal.
